key_insight: Cold-start PV forecasting can be made feasible by generating a synthetic site history from metadata and weather, then conditioning time-series foundation models at inference time.
engineering_relevance: This enables PV operators to produce early forecasts at commissioning without waiting for local historical measurements, improving deployment readiness for new plants.
method: Create physics-informed synthetic production histories from plant metadata and meteorological covariates.
Feed the synthetic history into five time-series foundation models for zero-shot forecasting.
Benchmark against classical baselines under Cold-Start Baseline, Real Feedback, and Self-Forecast Feedback settings.
evidence_signal: Across 440 PV sites in four datasets, covariate-aware foundation models beat baselines by about 1.7–2×, with TabPFN-TS best under Real Feedback and Chronos-2 most robust under Self-Forecast Feedback.
watch_item: Results suggest the pipeline depends more on having plausible temporal context than on the exact synthetic-history generator, so production deployment should verify generator stability across new climates and site types.
paper_title: Time series Foundation Models based on Physics-Informed Synthetic Histories for Cold-Start Photovoltaic Forecasting
